pro_course_detail.title: Conversational English
pro_course_detail.description:
This lesson is for those of you who wish to practice and improve your fluency, pronunciation and vocabulary. During the lesson we will talk about a range of subjects. This can be focused on any area you wish from the weather to work, films to theatre, business to travel and anything and everything between these examples. 
I will correct your pronunciation, grammar accent and fluency during these lessons as well as explaining new vocabulary.

pro_course_detail.description:
During the lesson we will discuss business related topics. I can offer a structured package of lessons or tailor make the lessons to your individual need. We will look at every aspect of the business world and the related terminology and verbal phrases related to these. 
We can practice applying the phrases and terms in roleplay scenarios, applying them to sentences and conversations. There will of course be plenty of time to practice small talk, the glue that holds any business together. 
We can also practice and prepare for job interviews either as part of this course or separately.

pro_course_detail.title: Guided reading & discussions
pro_course_detail.description:
During the lesson you will reading text from a range of agreed areas and themes. You will be asked to summarize the text read. And then there will be discussion related to topics within the text. 
During each lesson I will correct each pronunciation error, explain new vocabulary and encourage you to use this within a conversation in order to more fully understand the words.

pro_course_detail.title: Job Applications and Job Interview preparation
pro_course_detail.description:
We can develop your resume in order to make sure it is as effective as it can be. We will look at every aspect of the resume from layout to language used. 
We will cover approaches to increase your chances of success in getting to the interview stage.
As I have gained many years of experience interviewing candidates from the employer perspective and also supported and prepared many individuals at all levels for the interview, I feel that I have a wealth of experience and knowledge to share with you so come and let me help you to achieve your career goals.
I will prepare you for the job interview. During our classes we will roleplay the interview and I will ask you real interview questions. I will then give you feedback and advice so as to help you to improve your responses.

pro_course_detail.title: Meeting or presentation preparation
pro_course_detail.description:
We will look at how you can improve you presentation skills. If you already have material, you have to present or prepare for presentation we will look at how to make this more effective. Then we will practice delivering this in order for you to become more confident, sound more fluent and professional.
If you don't yet have material, I can give you material to practice with or set homework for to build and then improve material in order to improve your skills.

Essential words promote clearer communication. By using widely understood

Essential words are often familiar to a broad audience. Utilizing them
increases the likelihood that listeners or readers will understand the content, preventing
misunderstandings.

In diverse settings, essential words provide a common ground for speakers of different backgrounds. This is particularly important in multicultural environments where not everyone may be fluent in English.

Efficiency: 
Essential words help convey ideas succinctly. This is especially valuable in
professional settings, where time is often limited, and clear communication is needed.
Accessibility: Using essential vocabulary makes information more accessible to individuals
who may be learning English or have lower proficiency levels. It encourages inclusivity in
communication.

Engagement:
When essential words are used effectively, they can engage the audience more readily. Familiar terms resonate better, making it easier for listeners to connect with the
message.

Foundation for Learning: 
For English language learners, a strong grasp of essential vocabulary forms the foundation for more complex language acquisition. Mastery of basic
words enable learners to build upon their language skills.

Cultural Relevance: 
Certain essential words may carry specific cultural meanings or connotations, which can enhance the richness of communication. Understanding these terms can deepen cross-cultural understanding

pro_course_detail.title: Sound like a Native with the American English Mouth Posture!
pro_course_detail.description:
READ FIRST: I only accept serious students who will make time outside of class and put in the work required. I will guide you and give you the tools and techniques you need, but your results are mostly dependent on you. This isn't a traditional class where you show up, do a few exercises, and then forget about it until the next lesson.

OUTLINE

We're changing the SETTINGS of how you hold the vocal tract underneath the sounds, meaning that it's less about producing certain sounds (which will also be covered) and more about maintaining the correct settings at all times. That's the main thing that creates the accent, not the sounds.

This course has a few phases:

Phase 0: You'll become aware of your tongue and overall vocal tract, as well as your native posture. If needed, this will include special exercises designed to help you get better control over different parts of the tongue and throat. Phase 0 overlaps with phase 1.


Phase 1: We'll use the House Framework to build the core of the American posture, the foundation for everything else. This includes the schwa/UH/center of gravity. We'll also start working on breathing.


Phase 2: We'll use various techniques and exercises as we go through 2 sections to build the sounds with the posture and slowly start linking things together into syllables, words, and sentences. We'll also add linking, stress, etc as we go, but these are not a main focus in the beginning. 99% of people underestimate the work we're doing and want to jump right to words and sentences, but that's exactly the same as trying to run when you haven't learned to walk.

-SECTION 1 SOUNDS (mostly front):
T/D/N, S/Z, K/G/NG, AW (cot/caught), Y, EE, IH, EH, AH (cat), EI, AI

-SECTION 2 SOUNDS (mostly lips and back): F/V, P/B/M, SH/ZH, CH/J, TH/TH, W, U, O, UUH (book), OW, OI


Phase 3 (new centers of gravity): R (both + R-colored), L (both + L-colored). The R and dark L (mostly) take over the center of gravity and also "color"/blend with various sounds.

pro_course_detail.title: General Pronunciation Lessons (NOT Mouth Posture Course)
pro_course_detail.description:
This class is for anyone who wants to work on their American accent WITHOUT mouth posture. It is NOT possible to have a perfect accent without mouth posture. In addition, the mouth posture approach also makes things easier overall (though it might seem harder in the short term). However, if you just want to sound better/clearer (not perfect or near perfect) and/or you just want to improve certain areas of pronunciation such as stress or linking, then this class is for you. However, I do NOT teach advanced intonation. Basic intonation patterns are fine, but advanced intonation is a tricky topic that I dislike teaching. The exact content we focus on can be tailored to your needs, goals, and interests.

Note that the mouth posture class contains all areas of pronunciation, but things like stress, linking, and rhythm come little by little as we move through the course and are not the main focus, especially in the beginning. Please see the mouth posture course for more information. It is STRONGLY recommended that you at least learn the basic components of mouth posture because it helps everything else, especially the formation and clarity of individual sounds (and will also improve your listening indirectly). We can include these basics in this class if desired.

We can also do any ear training you might need, including hearing the difference between certain sounds, properly hearing the stress, and more.

1-hour classes at least twice a week is recommended, but not required.

Lastly, I do NOT teach beginners. You must have at least a B1/lower-intermediate level. B2/upper-intermediate is preferred. For B1 and B2 students (especially B1), these classes will also drastically improve your listening skills.
